paragraphs.text: A rolled [GABA oolong](gaba:definition) from Taiwan. GABA names a way of making tea rather than a plant or a place: the leaf is treated so that the finished tea holds far more of this amino acid than ordinary tea does. The fresh leaf first spends some hours [without oxygen](gaba:making), sealed in a chamber filled with nitrogen or emptied to a vacuum. Without air it turns its glutamic acid into GABA and cannot break it down again, so it builds up. After that it is made as any [oolong](oolong:definition) is: withered and tossed, fixed, rolled and dried.

The [method began in Japan](gaba:history) and is dated to 1987. Taiwan's tea research station later changed it and adapted it to oolong, and the island is now a main source of GABA tea sold abroad. The label names only [Taiwan](taiwan:on-a-label). That tells you the leaf was grown on the island and nothing more about its mountain, height or cultivar.

brewing.text: In a cup or pot, steep it for about two to five minutes. It is forgiving of small changes in water temperature and steeping time. It can also be cold-brewed, steeped for some hours in the fridge.

notice.text: Ripe, dried or stewed fruit such as apricot, honeyed sweetness, a smooth, round body, and little bitterness or astringency; often brown sugar or roasted grain, sometimes wood or spice, and a light fruity sourness.
